name: MAX-M10S-00B
title: MAX-M10S: u-blox M10 standard-precision L1 GNSS receiver module, professional grade
summary: A 10.1 × 9.7 × 2.5 mm, 18-pad castellated GNSS receiver built on the u-blox M10 platform (UBX-M10050-KB chip) with a TCXO, an RTC crystal, a band-13 notch, an LNA and a SAW filter ahead of the chip. It tracks GPS/QZSS, Galileo, GLONASS and BeiDou on L1 at once (four systems concurrently), takes a passive or active antenna on RF_IN, and talks UBX and NMEA over UART and I2C. Main supply runs from 1.76 to 3.6 V, with a separate I/O supply set to 1.8 V or 3.3 V by the VIO_SEL pin and a backup supply. Continuous tracking takes about 25 mW.
key_figures: 9.5 mA typ at 3.0 V, default constellations

notes: Both ordering codes are u-blox M10 GNSS receiver modules, professional grade: MAX-M10S-00B is the global variant, MAX-M10S-00B1 the regional variant.

Name fields: PPP form factor (MAX), TGG platform (M10), V variant (S: standard precision, ROM, TCXO, LNA and SAW filter), NN major product version (00, 01, 02, ...), Q grade (A automotive, B professional), (R) production site (none for global, 1 for regional), XX hardware and firmware revision.
Product name PPP-TGGV (MAX-M10S); ordering code PPP-TGGV-NNQ(R) (MAX-M10S-00B, MAX-M10S-00B1); type number PPP-TGGV-NNQ(R)-XX (MAX-M10S-00B-01, MAX-M10S-00B1-01).

operation.text: RF_IN feeds a band-13 notch, an LNA and a SAW filter, then the UBX-M10050-KB chip with its own LNA, RF front end and fractional-N synthesizers. A TCXO and an RTC crystal clock the chip. VCC goes through a ferrite bead to the VCC_RF pin and through a DC-DC converter to the chip's power management; V_IO and V_BCKP go to the chip directly. The LNA_EN signal also reaches the module's front-end LNA.

Four GNSS can be tracked at once: GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou. From the factory the receiver runs GPS, Galileo and BeiDou B1I together, with QZSS and SBAS on. Fewer constellations may be configured to save power.

VIO_SEL picks the V_IO range. On a 1.8 V V_IO with V_BCKP supplied, hardware backup is entered by removing V_IO 100 ms before VCC; the other route is a UBX-RXM-PMREQ command into software standby, after which V_IO and VCC are removed. On 3 V supplies V_IO and VCC may drop together, or V_IO first.

When V_IO falls below about 1.45 V the backup domain moves its supply from V_IO to V_BCKP. Hardware backup is VCC and V_IO at 0 V with V_BCKP held up, drawing 28 µA typ; software standby keeps the supplies on and draws 37 to 46 µA from V_IO.

RESET_N has a 10 kΩ typ pull-up; holding it low for 1 ms or more resets the receiver, and during reset every PIO is an input with pull-up. SAFEBOOT_N low at start-up puts the receiver in safeboot mode; it shares PIO4 with TIMEPULSE through 1 kΩ.

The receiver communicates over UART and I2C. Inputs have internal pull-ups and may float when unused; PIO levels follow V_IO. The UART runs from 9600 to 921600 bit/s with no hardware flow control. I2C is a Fast-mode peripheral only (no Standard-mode, no controller role), up to 400 kHz, and may stretch SCL for up to 20 ms. The internal pull-ups can be very weak, so external pull-ups may be needed for 400 kbit/s.

The module's LNA and SAW filter serve passive-antenna designs for maximum sensitivity. LNA_EN switches an external LNA or active antenna on and off. RF_IN accepts up to 30 dB of external gain in the default low-gain mode, or 10 to 40 dB in bypass mode, and tolerates DC from -5.5 to +5.5 V; it has a DC block inside.
Continuous tracking uses about 25 mW. Inrush at power-up reaches 100 mA.
The module is pin-to-pin compatible with products of earlier u-blox generations.
Delivered on sealed reels: 500 per reel for MAX-M10S-00B, 1000 for MAX-M10S-00B1. Reflow soldered per IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020; MSL 4.
